findings.title: Allergy severity defaults to Unknown and stays active at go-live; the clinical design says the panel is empty and severity comes from the patient
findings.why_incompatible: FLLD-DM-04 (approved 14 January) migrates every legacy allergy into the active clinical panel, and where severity cannot be parsed sets it to "Unknown" while keeping the record active and visible. FLLD-CLIN-11 (approved 19 February) requires the same panel to be empty at go-live, forbids legacy data from populating a clinical field, and requires severity to be elicited from the patient at the first appointment. Both cannot be built.
findings.clinical_consequence: A patient with a documented anaphylaxis presents after go-live with the allergy shown as severity Unknown. The hard-stop that would force reconciliation exempts emergency orders, so an emergency prescription can be written against an Unknown severity record. The remedy the clinical design relies on, capture at first appointment, is the appointment the patient is already in.

findings.title: Unmapped legacy allergens are coded as No known allergy
findings.why_incompatible: The migration design and the field mapping both send any allergen that fails SNOMED matching to concept 716186003, No known allergy, with the original text demoted to a secondary note. The clinical design prohibits legacy data populating a clinical field at all. A coding fallback that asserts the absence of an allergy is the opposite of a blank.
findings.clinical_consequence: A real allergy whose legacy label did not match the subset is presented to prescribers as a positive statement that the patient has no known allergy. Drug-allergy interaction alerts cannot fire on a No known allergy record.

findings.title: Severity derivation was cancelled in a Teams channel and the mapping sheet; the approved design still mandates it
findings.why_incompatible: On 3 March the Pharmacy SME and Pharmacy Lead rejected regex severity derivation, Row 6 of the field mapping was set to Migrate=N, the joint walkthrough was cancelled without minutes, and nobody raised a change request. FLLD-DM-04 v3.0 remains the approved artefact and still contains DM-04-R04 and DM-04-R05 as active requirements.
findings.clinical_consequence: An ETL developer working from the approved design builds severity derivation and the Unknown default; a mapping technician working from the CSV suppresses the field. Which one ships depends on who reads which document. The authoritative record of the decision is a chat message.

findings.title: Ward location codes migrate through a lookup that no approved design defines
findings.why_incompatible: Row 12 of the field mapping is set to migrate WARD_LOCATION_CODE via a Ward Master reference. The channel confirms no design document exists for ward-level translation and the item was parked pending the PAS team.
findings.clinical_consequence: Inpatient allergy records whose legacy ward code has no translation either reject at load or attach to the wrong care setting, and the exception queue has 72 hours to clear them.

findings.title: A paediatric safeguarding note sits at the end of a free-text field that Row 10 truncates, and nobody in the programme owns it
findings.why_incompatible: Row 10 truncates CLINICAL_COMMENTS at 4000 characters. The Pharmacy Lead identified that a safeguarding flag is held only in that free text, at the end, and asked who owns it. The migration architect declined ownership and redirected the question out of the channel. No document records a decision.
findings.clinical_consequence: A child's safeguarding flag is silently removed by the migration. The paediatric verification flag in DM-04-R08 does not cover it because the flag is not a coded allergy field.
